1	"""Deterministic 2D grid A* planner.
2	
3	Public entry points: ``plan(width, height, blocked, start, goal, costs=None,
4	trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
5	max_cost=None, allow_wait=False, dynamic_costs=None, reservations=None)``,
6	``plan_any(width, height, blocked,
7	start, goals, costs=None, trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None,
8	max_expanded=None, snapshot=False, max_cost=None, allow_wait=False,
9	dynamic_costs=None, reservations=None)``,
10	``plan_k(width, height, blocked, start, goal, k, costs=None,
11	dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, max_cost=None,
12	allow_wait=False, dynamic_costs=None, reservations=None)``,
13	``plan_batch(width, height, blocked, requests, costs=None, trace=False,
14	dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
15	max_cost=None, allow_wait=False, dynamic_costs=None, reservations=None)``,
16	``plan_multi_start(width, height, blocked, starts, goal, costs=None,
17	trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
18	max_cost=None, allow_wait=False, dynamic_costs=None, reservations=None)``,
19	``replay(width, height, blocked, start, goal, path, costs=None,
20	dynamic_blocked=None, diagnose=False, allow_wait=False,
21	dynamic_costs=None, reservations=None)``,
22	``resume(checkpoint, max_expanded=None)``,
23	``distance_field(width, height, blocked, goal, costs=None, trace=False)``
24	and
25	``distance_field_any(width, height, blocked, goals, costs=None,
26	trace=False)``.
27	
28	Semantics:
29	- Four-neighborhood moves, Manhattan heuristic. Without ``costs`` each step
30	  has unit cost. With ``costs`` (a height-by-width matrix of positive
31	  integers, row-major: ``costs[y][x]``) entering a cell costs that cell's
32	  value; the start cell's cost is never counted, so ``cost`` is the sum of
33	  the costs of the cells entered along the path.
34	- Tie-breaking is fully specified and order-independent: compare f, then h,
35	  then the (x, y) coordinate in lexicographic order.
36	- ``expanded`` counts exactly the nodes popped from the priority queue and
37	  closed for the first time (the goal counts when reached; stale heap
38	  entries and duplicate closings do not).
39	- Returns ``{"path": [...], "cost": int, "expanded": int}`` on success and
40	  ``{"path": None, "cost": None, "expanded": int}`` when unreachable.
41	- When ``trace`` is true, both kinds of results additionally include
42	  ``expanded_nodes``: the list of coordinate tuples closed for the first
43	  time, in expansion order (includes the start, and the goal on success);
44	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)``. The field is omitted entirely when
45	  ``trace`` is false or omitted.
46	
47	Search budget (``max_expanded``):
48	- ``max_expanded`` may be omitted or ``None``, which keeps every key,
49	  value, exception type and validation order of the default behavior
50	  untouched. Otherwise it must be a non-negative integer that is not a
51	  bool: other types raise ``TypeError`` and negative values raise
52	  ``ValueError``. These checks run after all existing grid, costs,
53	  ``trace`` and ``dynamic_blocked`` validation (including the frame-0
54	  check) and before the search starts.
55	- The budget counts closed nodes (exactly what ``expanded`` counts); once
56	  the limit is reached no further node is closed. When the budget is
57	  provided the result always carries an additional ``status`` field:
58	  ``"found"`` when the goal was closed within the limit (the usual
59	  ``path``/``cost`` are returned), ``"unreachable"`` when the candidates
60	  were exhausted without reaching the goal, and ``"budget_exhausted"``
61	  when live candidates remained but the budget stopped the search (then
62	  ``path``/``cost`` are ``None`` and ``expanded`` is the actual closed
63	  count, at most ``max_expanded``).
64	- The budget applies identically in static and dynamic mode and never
65	  changes expansion order, path choice, trace entries or determinism: a
66	  budgeted trace is a prefix of the unbudgeted one. With ``trace=True``
67	  only actually closed nodes are recorded, so a zero budget records
68	  nothing -- even when ``start == goal`` a zero budget returns
69	  ``budget_exhausted`` with ``expanded == 0``; the single-point success
70	  result requires at least one closed node (``max_expanded >= 1``).
71	- ``replay`` is unaffected: it keeps validating candidate paths only and
72	  accepts no budget parameter.
73	
74	Cost limit (``max_cost``):
75	- ``max_cost`` may be omitted or ``None``, which keeps every key, value,
76	  exception type and validation order of the previous behavior untouched.
77	  Otherwise it must be a non-negative integer that is not a bool: other
78	  types raise ``TypeError`` and negative values raise ``ValueError``. The
79	  check runs after all existing grid, costs, ``trace``, ``dynamic_blocked``,
80	  ``max_expanded`` and ``snapshot`` validation and before the search
81	  starts.
82	- The limit caps the accumulated entering-cell cost of a route, measured
83	  from the start (the start cell still costs 0 and each entered cell costs
84	  its ``costs`` value, or 1 without ``costs``). A candidate whose
85	  accumulated cost would exceed the limit is discarded; a candidate at
86	  exactly the limit still competes. The limit applies identically in
87	  static mode, dynamic mode and ``plan_any``, and never changes expansion
88	  order, tie-breaks, the minimum-cost choice, the multi-goal endpoint
89	  comparison or trace entries.
90	- When ``max_cost`` is provided the result always carries ``status``:
91	  ``"found"`` on success, and on failure ``"cost_exhausted"`` when at
92	  least one candidate was discarded for exceeding the limit, otherwise
93	  ``"unreachable"`` (``path``/``cost`` are ``None`` and ``expanded``
94	  counts the actually closed nodes). When ``max_expanded`` is also given,
95	  a budget stop still takes priority with ``"budget_exhausted"``.
96	  ``trace`` keeps recording only actually closed nodes, and the
97	  ``start == goal`` single-point zero-cost result and the zero-budget
98	  rules are unchanged.
99	- With ``snapshot=True`` the checkpoint records the ``max_cost`` value
100	  when one was provided (and no new field when it was not). ``resume``
101	  treats a checkpoint without the field as ``None``, validates a present
102	  field with the same rules (``TypeError`` for wrong types, ``ValueError``
103	  for negative values or a state inconsistent with the limit) before any
104	  searching, and a resumed search is equivalent to one uninterrupted call
105	  with the same limit. ``replay`` accepts no ``max_cost`` parameter.
106	
107	Waiting in place (``allow_wait``):
108	- ``plan``, ``plan_any``, ``plan_batch``, ``plan_multi_start``, ``plan_k``
109	  and ``replay`` accept a final optional boolean ``allow_wait`` that
110	  defaults to ``False``. ``False`` -- or an omitted, ``None`` or empty
111	  ``dynamic_blocked`` -- keeps every key, value, exception type,
112	  validation order, four-neighborhood move, no-repeated-coordinate rule
113	  and tie-break of the previous behavior untouched. A non-bool
114	  ``allow_wait`` raises ``TypeError`` after the ``dynamic_blocked``
115	  checks (the frame-0 check included) and before the budget and snapshot
116	  checks; every other exception type and order is unchanged.
117	- With ``allow_wait=True`` a route may stay in its current cell from
118	  time ``t`` to time ``t + 1`` provided the cell is not blocked at frame
119	  ``t + 1``. Waiting adds no entering-cell cost (``cost`` still sums
120	  only the cells entered by moves, and ``max_cost`` caps only those) and
121	  is only generated while ``t + 1`` lies within the provided frames:
122	  after the last frame the last frame is still reused for moves but no
123	  further waits are generated. Consecutive waits repeat the same
124	  coordinate in the path; once a cell is left it may never be
125	  re-entered. ``start == goal`` still yields only the single-point
126	  zero-cost route.
127	- The minimum-cost choice, the endpoint selection and the complete-path
128	  lexicographic tie-break follow the existing rules, with the priority
129	  still f, then h, then the coordinate, then the time and finally the
130	  complete path, so results never depend on obstacle-set or in-frame
131	  iteration order. Wait states count toward ``expanded`` one per closing
132	  and the trace records their ``(x, y, t)`` triples; ``max_expanded``
133	  truncates them like any other state and the ``status`` values and
134	  priorities are unchanged. ``plan_k``, ``plan_batch``, multi-goal and
135	  multi-start results follow the same waiting semantics, and a
136	  successful path verifies in ``replay`` with the same cost and step
137	  count, the waits included in ``steps``.
138	- ``replay`` with ``allow_wait=True`` accepts consecutive stays only
139	  within the provided dynamic frames; stays in static mode or without
140	  frames, stays after the final frame and non-consecutive revisits all
141	  return the usual invalid structure. With ``diagnose=True`` a stay
142	  after the final frame reports the dedicated error
143	  ``wait_after_final_frame``.
144	- A budget-exhausted checkpoint records ``allow_wait`` when it was true
145	  and ``resume`` of such a checkpoint is equivalent to one uninterrupted
146	  call with the same setting. Checkpoints written without the field
147	  restore it as ``False``; a present non-bool field raises ``TypeError``
148	  and a field inconsistent with the recorded internal state raises
149	  ``ValueError``.
150	
151	Dynamic obstacles (``dynamic_blocked``):
152	- ``dynamic_blocked`` may be omitted, ``None`` or an empty sequence, which
153	  leaves the static behavior above untouched. Otherwise it must be a
154	  sequence of frames; each frame is an iterable of grid coordinates that
155	  are blocked at that time frame. Frame 0 constrains ``start``; the
156	  coordinate at path index ``t`` must avoid both the static obstacles and
157	  frame ``t``, and frames beyond the last one reuse the last frame.
158	- Moves are still four-neighborhood only: no waiting in place and no
159	  repeated coordinates along the path. Because feasibility of a route
160	  depends on the coordinates it already visited, candidates that reach the
161	  same ``(x, y, t)`` through different coordinate histories are distinct
162	  states and are never merged: every route that satisfies the constraints
163	  can be explored. ``cost`` is still the sum of the costs of the cells
164	  entered; the start cell is never counted.
165	- The minimum-cost feasible route is returned. When total costs tie, the
166	  fixed priority is f, then h, then x, y, t, and candidates still tied are
167	  ordered lexicographically by their complete coordinate sequence, so the
168	  result never depends on the iteration order of the obstacle sets, the
169	  coordinates inside a frame, or the traversal order.
170	- In dynamic mode ``expanded_nodes`` records ``(x, y, t)`` triples in
171	  actual closing order and ``expanded`` counts closed space-time route
172	  states one per entry; a discarded candidate is never recorded. When the
173	  same ``(x, y, t)`` is closed through different histories, its triple
174	  appears once per closing in closing order, and ``expanded`` counts each
175	  such entry. On failure ``path``/``cost`` are ``None``.
176	- Validation: the outer value must be a sequence and every frame an
177	  iterable of coordinates; strings/bytes and non-two-integer coordinates
178	  raise ``TypeError``, out-of-bounds coordinates raise ``ValueError``,
179	  duplicates within a frame are merged, and a ``start`` blocked at frame 0
180	  raises ``ValueError``. All checks run before the search starts.
181	
182	Time-varying costs (``dynamic_costs``):
183	- ``plan``, ``plan_any``, ``plan_batch``, ``plan_multi_start``,
184	  ``plan_k`` and ``replay`` accept a final optional
185	  ``dynamic_costs=None`` parameter. Omitting it, passing ``None`` or an
186	  empty sequence keeps every result key, exception boundary, expansion
187	  order, path choice and the legacy ``costs`` semantics of the previous
188	  behavior untouched; every other entry point keeps its signature.
189	- Otherwise ``dynamic_costs`` must be a sequence of height-by-width
190	  matrices of positive integers, one matrix per time frame. An outer
191	  value or frame that is not an acceptable sequence, or a cell that is
192	  not a non-bool integer, raises ``TypeError``; a wrong row or column
193	  count, a non-positive cost, or providing both ``costs`` and
194	  ``dynamic_costs`` raises ``ValueError``. All checks run after every
195	  pre-existing validation (in ``plan_batch`` before any request is
196	  searched) and before the search starts.
197	- When enabled, entering a coordinate at path index ``t`` costs that
198	  cell's value in frame ``t``; the start cell is still never charged and
199	  frames beyond the last one reuse the last frame. Waiting follows the
200	  existing rules and never produces an entering-cell cost. The search
201	  returns the globally minimum total ``cost`` route under the static and
202	  dynamic obstacle constraints; equal costs are still arbitrated by the
203	  existing endpoint and complete-path lexicographic rules, and
204	  ``expanded``/``expanded_nodes`` count only actually closed space-time
205	  states: distinct histories are never merged and no out-of-bounds,
206	  blocked or illegally repeated nodes are generated.
207	- ``max_cost`` caps the dynamic accumulated cost with the usual
208	  ``cost_exhausted`` and budget-priority rules; ``plan_any``'s winning
209	  endpoint rules, the trace shape, the ``start == goal`` result and
210	  unreachable results are unchanged. ``plan_batch`` answers each
211	  request exactly as an independent ``plan`` call with the same frames;
212	  ``plan_multi_start`` picks its winner by the same total-cost and
213	  complete-path tie-breaks and records ``(x, y, t)`` trace triples in
214	  dynamic mode; ``plan_k`` ranks its unique routes by the dynamic
215	  accumulated cost with the usual truncation and status rules.
216	  ``replay`` recomputes ``cost``
217	  with the same frames, so a legal path matches the planning result;
218	  the diagnostic error types and the ``steps`` rule are unchanged.
219	- With ``snapshot=True`` the checkpoint records ``dynamic_costs`` as a
220	  JSON-serializable structure (the field is omitted when they were not
221	  provided) together with the waiting setting, the accumulated state and
222	  the cost limit when one was provided; a resumed search matches one
223	  uninterrupted call field by field, the next checkpoint included. A
224	  checkpoint whose ``dynamic_costs`` is corrupt raises ``TypeError`` or
225	  ``ValueError`` and never silently degrades. ``plan_k`` accepts no
226	  snapshot option.
227	
228	Reserved space-time routes (``reservations``):
229	- ``plan``, ``plan_any``, ``plan_batch``, ``plan_multi_start``,
230	  ``plan_k`` and ``replay`` accept a final optional
231	  ``reservations=None`` parameter for multi-robot coordination.
232	  Omitting it, passing ``None`` or an empty sequence keeps every result
233	  key, exception type, validation order, expansion order and tie-break
234	  of the previous behavior untouched; existing calls need no changes.
235	- Otherwise ``reservations`` must be a sequence of non-empty coordinate
236	  paths, each the timed route another agent already occupies. An outer
237	  value or path that is not an acceptable sequence, or a coordinate
238	  that is not exactly two integers, raises ``TypeError``; an empty
239	  path, an out-of-bounds coordinate, a coordinate on a static obstacle
240	  or a coordinate repeated non-consecutively within one path raises
241	  ``ValueError``. Consecutive stays inside a reservation path are
242	  kept. Duplicate routes merge and the entry order never influences
243	  any result. All checks run after every pre-existing validation (in
244	  ``plan_batch`` before any request is searched) and before the search
245	  starts.
246	- A path's t-th coordinate occupies that vertex at frame ``t``; past
247	  the final coordinate the last one persists. Each pair of adjacent
248	  coordinates forms the directed edge of that frame. A candidate route
249	  may not enter a reserved vertex at the same frame, nor traverse the
250	  reverse of a reserved edge between two frames. The candidate remains
251	  subject to the static obstacles, ``dynamic_blocked``, ``costs`` and
252	  ``dynamic_costs`` exactly as before, and reservations alone already
253	  make the search time-expanded.
254	- With ``allow_wait=True`` a route may wait in place at frames that are
255	  safe (the cell is neither blocked nor reserved at the next frame);
256	  waiting adds no entering-cell cost and is only generated while the
257	  next time step still lies within the provided frames (dynamic
258	  obstacle frames and reservation frames each provide them). Once a
259	  cell is left it may never be re-entered non-consecutively.
260	- Route selection keeps the dynamic-mode adjudication: smallest total
261	  ``cost``, then the arrival step count, then the complete coordinate
262	  sequence lexicographically. ``expanded`` counts only actually closed
263	  space-time states and ``trace`` records ``(x, y, t)`` triples; an
264	  unreachable query returns the usual empty-path result. A start
265	  reserved at frame 0 roots no feasible route.
266	- ``max_expanded``, ``max_cost``, ``plan_k``, ``plan_batch`` and
267	  ``plan_multi_start`` keep their ``status``, truncation and
268	  independent-query semantics. With ``snapshot=True`` the checkpoint
269	  records the normalized reservations (the field is omitted when they
270	  were not provided), and ``resume`` of such a checkpoint matches one
271	  uninterrupted call field by field; a checkpoint whose
272	  ``reservations`` is corrupt raises ``TypeError`` or ``ValueError``.
273	- ``replay`` re-checks a candidate path against the same reservations:
274	  a successful path verifies with the same ``cost`` and ``steps``.
275	  With ``diagnose=True`` a path entering a reserved vertex reports
276	  ``reservation_vertex`` and a path traversing a reserved edge in
277	  reverse reports ``reservation_edge``, each with the zero-based index
278	  of the first offending element; every other invalid path keeps the
279	  existing fixed structure and error codes.
280	
281	Multi-goal planning (``plan_any``):
282	- ``plan_any(width, height, blocked, start, goals, ...)`` accepts the same
283	  grid, blocked, start, costs, trace, dynamic_blocked and max_expanded
284	  arguments as ``plan``, plus a non-empty ``goals`` sequence of candidate
285	  endpoint coordinates. It returns one deterministic minimum-cost route to
286	  any of the candidates, in the same result structure as ``plan``; the
287	  path's last point is the winning endpoint.
288	- The grid, costs, trace, dynamic-blocked and budget checks run in
289	  ``plan``'s order with the same exception types; ``goals`` takes
290	  ``goal``'s position in that sequence. The outer value must be a
291	  sequence: strings, bytes, ``None`` and other non-sequences raise
292	  ``TypeError`` and an empty sequence raises ``ValueError``. Each endpoint
293	  follows the coordinate structure and integer rules (bad shape or
294	  coordinate types raise ``TypeError``); out-of-bounds coordinates and
295	  endpoints on static obstacles raise ``ValueError``. Repeated candidates
296	  merge, so the input ordering never changes any result.
297	- The search keeps four-neighborhood moves, no waiting, no revisits, the
298	  persistent last frame and the entering-cell cost accumulation. A
299	  candidate blocked by the dynamic frame at the time a particular route
300	  arrives is not rejected up front (its coordinate is statically valid);
301	  that arrival is simply infeasible for that route's time frame while
302	  other arrival times still compete.
303	- Total ``cost`` decides; ties compare the endpoint coordinate ``(x, y)``
304	  lexicographically, then the complete coordinate path lexicographically.
305	  As in dynamic ``plan``, routes reaching the same cell through different
306	  coordinate histories are distinct states and are never merged, so the
307	  traversal is a best-first walk of the feasible route tree; expansion
308	  order and the trace never depend on goal order, the blocked sets or
309	  in-frame iteration order. A budget never replaces an already determined
310	  better route with a worse one.
311	- When no endpoint is reachable, ``path`` and ``cost`` are ``None``. With a
312	  budget the ``status`` field follows the same ``"found"``,
313	  ``"unreachable"`` and ``"budget_exhausted"`` rules, and ``trace`` only
314	  records actually closed nodes: coordinate pairs in static mode and
315	  ``(x, y, t)`` triples in dynamic mode. A ``goals`` containing ``start``
316	  yields the single-point zero-cost route under the same start-equals-goal
317	  and zero-budget rules as ``plan``. A successful path verifies offline in
318	  ``replay`` when its last point is passed as ``goal``, with the same cost
319	  and step count.
320	
321	Top-k planning (``plan_k``):
322	- ``plan_k(width, height, blocked, start, goal, k, costs=None,
323	  dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, max_cost=None,
324	  allow_wait=False, dynamic_costs=None)`` returns
325	  several distinct feasible routes on the same grid in one call. It
326	  first performs exactly ``plan``'s shared validation for the
327	  dimensions, coordinates, static obstacles, positive integer cost
328	  matrix and dynamic frames (including the frame-0 start check), and
329	  only then checks ``k``: a non-bool positive integer is required,
330	  wrong types raise ``TypeError`` and non-positive values raise
331	  ``ValueError``. The optional ``max_expanded`` and ``max_cost``
332	  limits are checked after all of that (the ``k`` check included),
333	  still before the search starts, with the same non-negative,
334	  non-bool integer rules ``plan`` uses (other types raise
335	  ``TypeError``, negative values raise ``ValueError``). The optional
336	  ``dynamic_costs`` frames are validated after all of those checks,
337	  still before the search starts, with the shared time-varying cost
338	  rules (providing both ``costs`` and ``dynamic_costs`` raises
339	  ``ValueError``). Every error is
340	  decided before the search starts, and ``plan_k`` accepts no
341	  ``trace`` or ``snapshot`` argument.
342	- The search keeps four-neighborhood moves, the zero start cost, the
343	  entering-cell cost accumulation, the persistent last frame, the ban on
344	  waiting in place and on repeated coordinates, and the static/frame
345	  feasibility rules. Routes that reach the same cell through different
346	  coordinate histories are distinct candidates and are never merged, in
347	  both static and dynamic mode, so different complete coordinate
348	  sequences always remain separate results.
349	- It returns ``{"paths": [...], "costs": [...], "expanded": int}``: at
350	  most ``k`` unique complete routes ordered by ascending total cost and,
351	  on ties, by the lexicographic order of the complete coordinate
352	  sequence; ``costs`` corresponds to ``paths`` entry by entry. The first
353	  entry is the route ``plan`` would return. When no route is feasible
354	  both lists are empty and ``expanded`` still reports the route
355	  candidates actually closed to determine the answer: one count per
356	  complete history, and never counting a candidate filtered at
357	  generation or left pending. The traversal stops the moment the k-th
358	  goal route has been closed, so a small k closes strictly fewer
359	  candidates than a larger one. ``start == goal`` yields only the
360	  single-point zero-cost route, with one expansion. Every returned route
361	  verifies offline in ``replay`` with the same cost and step count, in
362	  both static and dynamic mode; the result never depends on obstacle-set
363	  iteration order, in-frame coordinate order or the traversal order.
364	- ``max_cost`` caps a route's accumulated entering-cell cost exactly as
365	  in ``plan``: the start still costs 0, a candidate exactly at the
366	  limit still competes and a candidate whose accumulated cost would
367	  exceed it is discarded the moment it is generated. It never changes
368	  the tie-break between legal routes. ``max_expanded`` caps the number
369	  of complete route candidates actually closed (exactly what
370	  ``expanded`` counts); once the limit is reached no further candidate
371	  is closed, and the limit only ever truncates the traversal -- it can
372	  never replace an already determined higher-ranked route. When either
373	  limit is provided the result additionally carries ``status``:
374	  ``"found"`` when all ``k`` routes were closed or the search exhausted
375	  naturally with at least one route; ``"budget_exhausted"`` when fewer
376	  than ``k`` routes were found and the budget stopped the search while
377	  candidates were still pending (this wins when both limits fire);
378	  ``"cost_exhausted"`` when fewer than ``k`` routes were found, no
379	  budget stop occurred and at least one candidate was discarded for the
380	  cost limit; ``"unreachable"`` when no route exists with neither a
381	  budget stop nor a cost discard. The routes already closed (and their
382	  costs, in rank order) are still returned when a limit ends the search
383	  early, as empty lists when none were found, and ``expanded`` is the
384	  actual closed count. Omitting both limits keeps every legacy key and
385	  value exactly unchanged.
386	
387	Batch planning (``plan_batch``):
388	- ``plan_batch(width, height, blocked, requests, costs=None,
389	  trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
390	  max_cost=None, allow_wait=False, dynamic_costs=None)`` answers
391	  several independent single-goal queries on
392	  one shared grid in a single call. It returns ``{"results": [...]}``
393	  with exactly the result ``plan`` would return for each query, in the
394	  order of ``requests``; duplicate requests are kept and each gets its
395	  own result.
396	- The shared arguments are validated with ``plan``'s rules and order,
397	  with ``requests`` taking the position of ``start``/``goal`` in that
398	  sequence. ``requests`` must be a non-empty sequence: ``None``,
399	  strings, bytes and other non-sequences raise ``TypeError`` and an
400	  empty sequence raises ``ValueError``. Each element must be a
401	  two-element sequence ``[start, goal]`` of grid coordinates: element
402	  shape or coordinate type failures raise ``TypeError``; out-of-bounds
403	  coordinates, endpoints on static obstacles and a start blocked at
404	  dynamic frame 0 raise ``ValueError``. Every check is decided before
405	  any search starts, so an invalid batch never returns partial results.
406	- Each query is an independent ``plan`` search over the shared grid:
407	  ``path``, ``cost`` and ``expanded`` are produced per request, and the
408	  ``max_expanded`` budget and the ``max_cost`` limit apply per query
409	  with no state shared across queries. The optional ``dynamic_costs``
410	  frames follow the shared time-varying cost rules and are validated
411	  after every other check, before any request is searched; each request
412	  is then answered exactly as an independent ``plan`` call with the
413	  same frames, and a per-request checkpoint records them. ``trace``,
414	  ``status``,
415	  ``expanded_nodes``, ``checkpoint``, dynamic frames, ``start == goal``,
416	  unreachable and ``cost_exhausted`` results all follow ``plan``
417	  exactly, and a returned ``checkpoint`` can be handed to ``resume``
418	  directly. A successful path ends at its request's goal and verifies
419	  offline in ``replay`` with the same cost and step count. The result
420	  never depends on obstacle-set iteration order, in-frame coordinate
421	  order or the permutation of ``requests``.

423	Multi-start planning (``plan_multi_start``):
424	- ``plan_multi_start(width, height, blocked, starts, goal, costs=None,
425	  trace=False, dynamic_blocked=None, max_expanded=None, snapshot=False,
426	  max_cost=None, allow_wait=False, dynamic_costs=None)`` plans from
427	  several candidate starts to one shared
428	  goal in a single call and returns one deterministic route, in exactly
429	  the result structure of ``plan``; the path begins at the winning start
430	  and ends at ``goal``. ``starts`` takes ``start``'s position in
431	  ``plan``'s validation sequence and every shared check keeps its order,
432	  exception type and message boundary.
433	- ``starts`` must be a non-empty sequence of grid coordinates: ``None``,
434	  strings, bytes and other non-sequences raise ``TypeError`` and an
435	  empty sequence raises ``ValueError``. Each start follows the
436	  coordinate structure and integer rules (bad shape or coordinate types
437	  raise ``TypeError``); out-of-bounds coordinates and starts on static
438	  obstacles raise ``ValueError``. Repeated starts merge and the tuple is
439	  sorted, so the input ordering never changes any result. A start
440	  blocked by dynamic frame 0 raises ``ValueError``; every check runs
441	  before the search starts.
442	- In static mode every start is a ``g == 0`` root and each coordinate is
443	  closed at most once: a cell keeps only its best known ``(cost, path)``
444	  pair (smallest accumulated entering-cell cost, then the
445	  lexicographically smallest complete coordinate sequence -- an ordering
446	  preserved under common extensions, so a dominated candidate can never
447	  win later). In dynamic mode the persistent last frame, the ban on
448	  waiting and on repeated coordinates apply, and routes reaching the
449	  same ``(x, y, t)`` through different coordinate histories are distinct
450	  states that are never merged. Time-varying ``dynamic_costs`` frames
451	  (validated after every other check, before the search) make the
452	  search time-expanded the same way obstacle frames do: entering a
453	  coordinate at path index ``t`` costs that frame's cell value, the
454	  last frame persists, and the trace records ``(x, y, t)`` triples.
455	- The winning route has the smallest total ``cost``; ties are decided by
456	  the lexicographic order of the complete coordinate path, so the result
457	  never depends on the input order of ``starts``. Expansion order is f,
458	  then h, then ``(x, y)`` (plus ``t`` in dynamic mode), and finally the
459	  complete path. ``cost`` counts only the cells entered (the winning
460	  start costs 0); ``expanded`` counts only closed candidates; when no
461	  route exists ``path`` and ``cost`` are ``None``.
462	- With ``trace=True`` static mode records the unique coordinate closing
463	  sequence and dynamic mode the ``(x, y, t)`` closing sequence, and
464	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)``. A ``starts`` entry equal to
465	  ``goal`` yields the single-point zero-cost route under the same
466	  start-equals-goal and zero-budget rules as ``plan``.
467	- ``max_expanded`` and ``max_cost`` follow ``plan``'s ``status`` and
468	  budget-priority rules: a candidate whose accumulated cost would
469	  exceed ``max_cost`` is discarded without counting toward ``expanded``,
470	  and neither limit ever changes the unlimited route or the tie-breaks.
471	  With ``snapshot=True`` a budget stop returns a JSON-serializable
472	  checkpoint recording the sorted starts, the grid constraints, the
473	  dynamic frames, the time-varying cost frames when they were provided,
474	  the cost limit when one was provided and the complete
475	  pending state; ``resume`` continues it with the cumulative-budget,
476	  no-double-counting and only-budget-exhausted-snapshots rules of the
477	  other planners, and invalid checkpoints follow ``resume``'s usual
478	  ``TypeError``/``ValueError`` boundaries.
479	
480	Snapshots and resumable planning (``snapshot`` and ``resume``):
481	- ``plan`` and ``plan_any`` accept a final ``snapshot=False`` option.
482	  Omitting it or passing ``False`` keeps every key, value, exception type,
483	  validation order, tie-break, unreachable result and trace of the
484	  previous behavior untouched. A non-bool ``snapshot`` raises
485	  ``TypeError`` after all existing checks (the ``max_expanded`` validation
486	  included) and before the search starts.
487	- With ``snapshot=True``, a search that stops because ``max_expanded``
488	  was reached (``status == "budget_exhausted"``) additionally returns
489	  ``checkpoint``: a fully JSON-serializable snapshot of the planner state.
490	  Results that already found the goal or proved it unreachable never
491	  carry the field.
492	- The checkpoint records the snapshot version, the planner kind, the
493	  normalized grid constraints (dimensions, obstacles, start, goal or
494	  candidate goals, costs, dynamic frames and the cost limit when one was
495	  provided), the closed-node count, the
496	  trace recorded so far and the complete pending-candidate state. Every
497	  set-derived list is stored sorted, so neither obstacle-set iteration
498	  order, goal order nor in-frame coordinate order influences the
499	  checkpoint's keys or values. A caller may store it as-is and hand it
500	  back to ``resume`` later.
501	- ``resume(checkpoint, max_expanded=None)`` continues the very same
502	  deterministic search described by the snapshot. ``max_expanded`` keeps
503	  its cumulative meaning: the total number of nodes that may be closed
504	  counted from the original start, so a limit not greater than the
505	  already closed count closes nothing more. The result is equivalent to
506	  one uninterrupted call with the same cumulative budget: ``path``,
507	  ``cost``, ``expanded``, ``status`` (present exactly when
508	  ``max_expanded`` is given) and ``expanded_nodes`` (always present in
509	  resume results; coordinate pairs in static mode, ``(x, y, t)`` triples
510	  in dynamic mode) all match, and repeated resumes never count an already
511	  closed node twice.
512	- When a resumed search reaches the budget again its result carries a
513	  fresh ``checkpoint`` that can be resumed in turn; ``found`` and
514	  ``unreachable`` results omit it. A successful resumed ``path`` verifies
515	  in ``replay`` with the same cost and step count.
516	- Validation: a checkpoint that is not an object, has missing required
517	  fields or wrongly typed fields raises ``TypeError``; an unsupported
518	  snapshot version or planner kind, grid constraints that violate the
519	  usual ``plan`` rules (obstacles, endpoints, costs, dynamic frames) or
520	  an internally inconsistent state raise ``ValueError``. Every check is
521	  decided before any searching, and ``resume``'s ``max_expanded`` follows
522	  the same non-negative-integer rules as ``plan``'s.
523	
524	Offline replay (``replay``):
525	- ``replay`` re-checks a saved candidate path without running any search;
526	  it never returns ``expanded`` or ``expanded_nodes``. It accepts the same
527	  grid arguments as ``plan`` (no ``trace``) plus ``path``.
528	- The grid arguments are validated with exactly the public ``plan``
529	  checks, and all of them run before the path is judged, so the same
530	  malformed grid inputs raise the same ``TypeError``/``ValueError``.
531	- ``path`` must be a non-empty sequence of grid coordinates; strings,
532	  bytes, ``None`` and other non-sequences raise ``TypeError``, as do
533	  elements that are not exactly two integers. Coordinates outside the
534	  grid raise ``ValueError``.
535	- A structurally valid but semantically invalid path does not raise: it
536	  returns ``{"valid": False, "cost": None, "steps": None}`` with no
537	  partial accumulation. Invalid means: not beginning at ``start``, not
538	  ending at ``goal``, visiting a static obstacle, visiting a cell blocked
539	  by frame ``t`` at path index ``t`` (the last frame persists for later
540	  indices; omitted/empty ``dynamic_blocked`` means static-only checks),
541	  non-four-neighbor adjacency, repeated coordinates, or extra points when
542	  ``start == goal``.
543	- A valid path returns ``{"valid": True, "cost": int, "steps": int}``
544	  where ``steps == len(path) - 1`` and ``cost`` is recomputed with the
545	  same entering-cell rule ``plan`` uses (sum of the costs of the cells
546	  entered; unit costs without ``costs``; the start cell is never
547	  counted), so it equals the cost ``plan`` assigns to that same path.
548	- ``diagnose`` defaults to false; omitting it or passing ``False`` keeps
549	  every key, value, exception type and validation order identical. A
550	  non-bool ``diagnose`` raises ``TypeError`` after all grid checks
551	  (including the frame-0 check) and before the path structure is
552	  inspected. With ``diagnose=True`` both results additionally carry
553	  ``error`` and ``error_index``: ``None``/``None`` for a valid path, and
554	  for an invalid one a single error code plus the zero-based index of
555	  the first offending element, with ``cost``/``steps`` still ``None``.
556	  The codes, in fixed precedence order, are ``start_mismatch`` (index
557	  0), ``goal_mismatch`` (index of the last element),
558	  ``start_goal_extra`` (index 1), ``repeated_coordinate`` (the second
559	  occurrence), ``non_adjacent`` (the later element of the pair),
560	  ``static_blocked`` and ``dynamic_blocked`` (the offending element);
561	  ties resolve to the earliest rule in this list and no partial cost is
562	  ever returned.
563	
564	Distance field (``distance_field``):
565	- ``distance_field(width, height, blocked, goal, costs=None,
566	  trace=False)`` is an offline analysis entry point for the static grid:
567	  it accepts only the dimensions, the static obstacles, a single goal and
568	  optionally ``costs`` and ``trace`` -- no start, no dynamic obstacles, no
569	  search budget, no cost limit and no snapshot option. The dimensions,
570	  goal coordinate, obstacle and costs checks (structure, integer types,
571	  bounds, duplicate merging, goal-on-obstacle) follow ``plan``'s public
572	  rules and order for those shared arguments and all run before the
573	  search starts; ``trace`` must be a bool (``TypeError`` otherwise).
574	- It returns ``{"distances": ..., "expanded": int}`` where ``distances``
575	  is a height-by-width matrix indexed ``distances[y][x]``: ``None`` for
576	  obstacles and for cells that cannot reach the goal, ``0`` for the goal
577	  itself, and for every other reachable cell the minimum sum of the
578	  entering-cell costs along a four-neighborhood route from that cell to
579	  the goal (unit steps without ``costs``; with ``costs`` each move adds
580	  the cost of the cell entered, exactly as ``plan`` accumulates ``cost``,
581	  so a reachable ``plan`` start yields the same value ``plan`` reports
582	  as ``cost``). No reachable distance is ever negative and the matrix
583	  always matches the grid dimensions; the result is JSON-serializable.
584	- ``expanded`` counts exactly the reachable cells determined and closed
585	  once each, the goal included. The closing order is fully specified:
586	  smallest current distance first, then the ``(x, y)`` coordinate in
587	  lexicographic order, so neither the obstacle-set iteration order nor
588	  the costs layout traversal influences the matrix, the count or the
589	  trace. With ``trace=True`` the result additionally carries
590	  ``expanded_nodes``, the coordinate pairs in that closing order, and
591	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)``; the field is omitted entirely
592	  when ``trace`` is false or omitted.
593	
594	Multi-goal distance field (``distance_field_any``):
595	- ``distance_field_any(width, height, blocked, goals, costs=None,
596	  trace=False)`` is the multi-goal counterpart of ``distance_field``:
597	  one offline analysis returns the minimum-cost field to any of the
598	  candidate endpoints in a single pass. It accepts only the dimensions,
599	  the static obstacles, a non-empty ``goals`` sequence and optionally
600	  ``costs`` and ``trace`` -- no start, no dynamic obstacles, no search
601	  budget, no cost limit and no snapshot option, and it never produces a
602	  ``status`` field. The dimensions, obstacles, costs and trace checks
603	  follow ``distance_field``'s public rules and order, and ``goals`` is
604	  validated exactly like ``plan_any``'s: ``None``, strings, bytes and
605	  other non-sequences raise ``TypeError``, an empty sequence raises
606	  ``ValueError``, elements that are not exactly two non-bool integers
607	  raise ``TypeError``, and out-of-bounds coordinates or endpoints on
608	  static obstacles raise ``ValueError``. The goals checks occupy
609	  ``goal``'s position in ``distance_field``'s validation sequence,
610	  duplicates merge, and every check runs before the search starts, so
611	  the input permutation never changes any result.
612	- It returns ``{"distances": ..., "targets": ..., "expanded": int}``.
613	  ``distances`` is the same height-by-width matrix as
614	  ``distance_field``: ``None`` for obstacles and for cells that cannot
615	  reach any endpoint, ``0`` for every endpoint, and otherwise the
616	  minimum over the endpoints of the accumulated entering-cell cost
617	  along a four-neighborhood route (unit steps without ``costs``; with
618	  ``costs`` each move adds the cost of the cell entered, the start
619	  cell's own cost never counted, exactly as ``plan``/``plan_any`` and
620	  ``distance_field`` accumulate). A reachable ``plan_any`` start yields
621	  the same value ``plan_any`` reports as ``cost``.
622	- ``targets`` is a matrix of the same shape: a reachable cell records
623	  the coordinate tuple of the endpoint that wins it, every other
624	  position is ``None`` (obstacles and unreachable cells, exactly where
625	  ``distances`` is ``None``); endpoints record themselves. When several
626	  endpoints tie at the same minimum distance the winner is the endpoint
627	  with the lexicographically smallest ``(x, y)`` coordinate, so the
628	  choice never depends on goal order. The whole result is
629	  JSON-serializable.
630	- ``expanded`` counts every reachable cell closed for the first time,
631	  all endpoints included, exactly once each. The closing order is
632	  smallest distance first, then the ``(x, y)`` coordinate
633	  lexicographically. With ``trace=True`` the result additionally
634	  carries ``expanded_nodes`` -- the coordinate pairs in that order,
635	  ``expanded == len(expanded_nodes)`` -- and the key is omitted
636	  entirely when ``trace`` is false or omitted.
637	
638	Validation (all performed before the search starts):
639	- ``width``/``height`` must be positive integers.
640	- ``start``, ``goal`` and every entry of ``blocked`` must be grid
641	  coordinates: sequences of exactly two integers (tuples, lists, etc.),
642	  normalized to tuples.
643	- ``goals`` (``plan_any`` and ``distance_field_any``) must be a
644	  non-empty sequence of grid coordinates following the same rules,
645	  normalized, deduplicated and order-independent.
646	- ``requests`` (``plan_batch``) must be a non-empty sequence of
647	  two-element ``[start, goal]`` coordinate pairs following the same
648	  coordinate rules, with the input order and duplicates preserved.
649	- ``costs`` may be omitted or ``None`` (unit costs). Otherwise it must be a
650	  sequence of ``height`` rows, each a sequence of ``width`` positive
651	  integers; strings/bytes, non-integer cells and booleans are rejected.
652	- ``dynamic_costs`` (``plan``, ``plan_any``, ``plan_batch``,
653	  ``plan_multi_start``, ``plan_k`` and ``replay``) may be
654	  omitted, ``None`` or an empty sequence. Otherwise it must be a
655	  sequence of frames, each frame a height-by-width matrix following the
656	  ``costs`` rules per frame; providing both ``costs`` and
657	  ``dynamic_costs`` raises ``ValueError``.
658	- ``reservations`` (``plan``, ``plan_any``, ``plan_batch``,
659	  ``plan_multi_start``, ``plan_k`` and ``replay``) may be
660	  omitted, ``None`` or an empty sequence. Otherwise it must be a
661	  sequence of non-empty coordinate paths; consecutive stays are kept,
662	  duplicate routes merge and the entry order never affects the result.
663	- ``trace`` must be a bool; non-bool values raise ``TypeError``.
664	- Type or structure violations raise ``TypeError``; non-positive
665	  dimensions, out-of-bounds coordinates, endpoints on obstacles, wrong
666	  matrix shape, or non-positive cell costs raise ``ValueError``.
667	- Duplicate blocked cells are merged without changing the result.
668	"""

685	def _is_int(value):
686	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)

689	def _validate_dimension(value, name):
690	    if not _is_int(value):
691	        raise TypeError(
692	            f"{name} must be an int, got {type(value).__name__}"
693	        )
694	    if value <= 0:
695	        raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a positive integer, got {value}")
696	    return value

699	def _normalize_point(value, name):
700	    if isinstance(value, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(value, Sequence):
701	        raise TypeError(
702	            f"{name} must be a sequence of two integers, "
703	            f"got {type(value).__name__}"
704	        )
705	    if len(value) != 2:
706	        raise TypeError(
707	            f"{name} must contain exactly two coordinates, got {len(value)}"
708	        )
709	    x, y = value[0], value[1]
710	    if not _is_int(x) or not _is_int(y):
711	        raise TypeError(f"{name} coordinates must be integers, got {value!r}")
712	    return (x, y)

715	def _check_bounds(point, width, height, name):
716	    x, y = point
717	    if not (0 <= x < width and 0 <= y < height):
718	        raise ValueError(
719	            f"{name} {point} is outside the {width}x{height} grid"
720	        )

723	def _normalize_blocked(blocked, width, height):
724	    if isinstance(blocked, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(blocked, Iterable):
725	        raise TypeError(
726	            f"blocked must be an iterable of grid coordinates, "
727	            f"got {type(blocked).__name__}"
728	        )
729	    cells = set()
730	    for index, item in enumerate(blocked):
731	        name = f"blocked[{index}]"
732	        point = _normalize_point(item, name)
733	        _check_bounds(point, width, height, name)
734	        cells.add(point)  # duplicates merge into one cell
735	    return cells

742	        raise TypeError(
743	            f"costs must be a height-by-width matrix of positive integers, "
744	            f"got {type(costs).__name__}"
745	        )
746	    if len(costs) != height:

748	            f"costs must have exactly {height} rows, got {len(costs)}"
749	        )

751	    for y, row in enumerate(costs):

930	def _reservation_frames(paths):
931	    # Compile normalized reservation paths into per-frame vertex and
932	    # directed-edge sets. A path's t-th coordinate occupies its vertex at
933	    # frame ``t``; past the final coordinate the last one persists, so
934	    # the last compiled frame (index ``R - 1`` with ``R`` the longest
935	    # path) doubles as the persistent tail, exactly like
936	    # ``dynamic_blocked``'s last frame. Frame ``t``'s edge set holds the
937	    # directed edges (p[t], p[t + 1]) of every path -- the move a
938	    # candidate makes between frames ``t`` and ``t + 1`` may not traverse
939	    # one of them in reverse. A stay or the persistent tail yields a
940	    # self-edge, which never constrains a moving candidate (its vertex is
941	    # reserved anyway).
942	    horizon = max(len(path) for path in paths)
943	    vertex_frames = []
944	    edge_frames = []
945	    for t in range(horizon):
946	        vertices = set()
947	        edges = set()
948	        for path in paths:
949	            current = path[t] if t < len(path) else path[-1]
950	            nxt = path[t + 1] if t + 1 < len(path) else path[-1]
951	            vertices.add(current)
952	            edges.add((current, nxt))
953	        vertex_frames.append(frozenset(vertices))
954	        edge_frames.append(frozenset(edges))
955	    return vertex_frames, edge_frames

958	def _goal_not_before(paths, goal):
959	    # The earliest frame at which a route may enter ``goal`` and then
960	    # occupy it forever, given that every path in ``paths`` keeps its own
961	    # final coordinate past its last frame: the frame after the last one
962	    # in which any of ``paths`` occupies the cell. ``None`` when no path
963	    # ever occupies it (no extra constraint); ``float("inf")`` when it is
964	    # some path's final coordinate, whose occupancy persists, so no
965	    # arrival can ever be safe.
966	    latest = None
967	    for path in paths:
968	        if path[-1] == goal:
969	            return float("inf")
970	        for t in range(len(path) - 1, -1, -1):
971	            if path[t] == goal:
972	                if latest is None or t > latest:
973	                    latest = t
974	                break
975	    return None if latest is None else latest + 1

1293	    the last one reuse the last frame); the start cell is never counted.
1294	    With ``reservations`` (normalized reservation paths) a candidate
1295	    route may not enter a vertex another agent occupies at the same
1296	    frame, nor traverse the reverse of a reserved directed edge between
1297	    two frames; reserved vertices persist at each path's final
1298	    coordinate. Waiting in place (unless ``allow_wait`` is set) and repeated
1299	    coordinates are forbidden, so
1300	    whether a candidate route can be
1301	    extended depends on the exact sequence of cells it already visited:
1302	    two routes reaching the same ``(x, y, t)`` with different histories
1303	    are distinct states and neither may prune the other (the route with
1304	    the larger accumulated cost can be the only one that remains
1305	    extendable). Each heap node therefore carries its complete path; the
1306	    search is a best-first traversal of the feasible route tree. Goal
1307	    closings are collected until the heap's smallest f exceeds the best
1308	    goal cost, after which the minimum-cost goal tie-break is settled by
1309	    the fixed f, h, x, y, t priority and then the complete path's
1310	    lexicographic order. With ``max_cost`` a candidate route whose
1311	    accumulated entering-cell cost would exceed the limit is discarded
1312	    (``cost_limited`` records that any discard happened, so a failure can
1313	    be reported as ``cost_exhausted``; the flag is part of the snapshot
1314	    state). With ``allow_wait`` a route may also stay in its current cell
1315	    for one frame at no entering-cell cost, generated only while the next
1316	    time step still lies within the provided frames and the cell is free
1317	    there; consecutive waits repeat the coordinate in the path, and once
1318	    a cell is left it may never be re-entered. With ``goal_not_before``
1319	    (used by ``plan_agents``) a route may not enter the goal cell before
1320	    that frame, because a reserved route still occupies it at some later
1321	    frame and the goal cell stays occupied once the route ends; such
1322	    candidates are never generated, exactly like reserved vertices.
1323	    With ``snapshot=True`` a
1324	    budget stop additionally
1325	    returns a checkpoint of the complete route-tree state; ``state``
1326	    carries such a snapshot back in for ``resume``.

1329	    def heuristic(point):
1330	        return abs(point[0] - goal[0]) + abs(point[1] - goal[1])
1331

1333	    last_cost_frame = len(cost_frames) - 1 if cost_frames is not None else None
1334	
1335	    def step_cost(point, t):
1336	        # Cost of entering ``point`` at time ``t``; the start cell is
1337	        # never entered. Time-varying frames take the value of frame
1338	        # ``t`` (the last frame persists); otherwise the static ``costs``
1339	        # matrix or unit steps apply.
1340	        if cost_frames is not None:
1341	            frame = (cost_frames[t] if t <= last_cost_frame
1342	                     else cost_frames[last_cost_frame])
1343	            return frame[point[1]][point[0]]
1344	        if costs is None:
1345	            return 1
1346	        return costs[point[1]][point[0]]
1347	
1348	    def frame_cells(t):
1349	        if frames is None:
1350	            return frozenset()
1351	        return frames[t] if t <= last_frame else frames[last_frame]
1352	
1353	    if reservations is not None:
1354	        vertex_frames, edge_frames = _reservation_frames(reservations)
1355	        last_res_frame = len(vertex_frames) - 1
1356	    else:
1357	        vertex_frames = edge_frames = last_res_frame = None
1358	
1359	    def reserved_vertices(t):
1360	        # Cells another agent occupies at frame ``t``; the final
1361	        # coordinate of every reservation path persists.
1362	        if vertex_frames is None:
1363	            return frozenset()
1364	        return (vertex_frames[t] if t <= last_res_frame
1365	                else vertex_frames[last_res_frame])
1366	
1367	    def reserved_edges(t):
1368	        # Directed edges (a, b) another agent traverses between frames
1369	        # ``t`` and ``t + 1``; a candidate may not move from ``b`` to
1370	        # ``a`` on that transition.
1371	        if edge_frames is None:
1372	            return frozenset()
1373	        return (edge_frames[t] if t <= last_res_frame
1374	                else edge_frames[last_res_frame])
1375	
1376	    # Waits may only enter provided frames: dynamic obstacle frames and
1377	    # reservation frames each provide them.
1378	    wait_last = _wait_horizon(frames, vertex_frames)
1379	
1380	    # Heap entries are (f, h, x, y, t, g, path, seen): f/h/x/y/t give the
1381	    # fixed numeric priority and candidates still tied are ordered by the
1382	    # complete coordinate path lexicographically, so ordering never depends
1383	    # on obstacle sets, in-frame coordinate order, or traversal order. The
1384	    # frozenset ``seen`` mirrors ``path`` for an O(1) repeat check and is
1385	    # never compared (distinct histories always differ in ``path``).

1389	        if reservations is not None and start in reserved_vertices(0):
1390	            # The root itself would occupy a reserved vertex at frame 0,
1391	            # so no feasible route exists.
1392	            open_heap = []
1393	        elif goal_not_before is not None and start == goal:
1394	            # The single-point route would occupy the goal cell from
1395	            # frame 0 on, but a reserved route still needs it later.
1396	            open_heap = []
1397	        else:

1399	                          frozenset(start_path))]
1400	        closed_count = 0
1401	        expanded_nodes = [] if trace or snapshot else None
1402	        cost_limited = False
1403	        # Best goal closing seen so far, keyed exactly as the tie-break
1404	        # specializes at the goal: (g, t, path) (there f == g, h == 0 and
1405	        # (x, y) is fixed). Closing a goal does not stop the search
1406	        # immediately: an equally cheap route whose chain runs through
1407	        # higher-h nodes might still be undeveloped. Since each move costs
1408	        # at least 1 and the Manhattan h changes by at most 1 per move,
1409	        # f = g + h never decreases along a route; once the smallest f on
1410	        # the heap exceeds the best goal cost, no route of that cost (or
1411	        # less) can remain undiscovered.

1415	        closed_count = state["closed_count"]
1416	        expanded_nodes = state["expanded_nodes"]
1417	        best_key = state["best_key"]
1418	        cost_limited = state["cost_limited"]

1420	    has_status = max_expanded is not None or max_cost is not None
1421

1423	        if best_key is not None and open_heap[0][0] > best_key[0]:
1424	            break
1425	        if max_expanded is not None and closed_count >= max_expanded:
1426	            # Live route candidates remain but the budget is spent; close
1427	            # nothing more. A goal already closed still wins below.
1428	            budget_stop = True
1429	            break
1430	        _, _, x, y, t, g, path, seen = heapq.heappop(open_heap)
1431	        closed_count += 1  # every popped route node closes exactly once
1432	        if expanded_nodes is not None:
1433	            # Histories reaching the same (x, y, t) each record a triple,
1434	            # in the order their route nodes are actually closed.
1435	            expanded_nodes.append((x, y, t))
1436	        if (x, y) == goal:
1437	            goal_key = (g, t, path)
1438	            if best_key is None or goal_key < best_key:
1439	                best_key = goal_key
1440	            continue  # routes end at the goal; never expanded past it
1441	        next_t = t + 1
1442	        frame = frame_cells(next_t)
1443	        reserved = reserved_vertices(next_t)
1444	        for dx, dy in _NEIGHBORS:
1445	            nx, ny = x + dx, y + dy
1446	            if not (0 <= nx < width and 0 <= ny < height):
1447	                continue
1448	            nxt = (nx, ny)
1449	            if nxt in obstacles or nxt in frame or nxt in seen:

1451	            if nxt in reserved:
1452	                continue  # vertex another agent occupies at frame next_t

1454	                    and next_t < goal_not_before):
1455	                # A reserved route still occupies the goal cell at some

1457	                # would keep the cell forever and be violated later.
1458	                continue

1462	            if max_cost is not None and new_g > max_cost:
1463	                # The candidate's accumulated cost exceeds the limit:
1464	                # discard it and remember that a discard happened.
1465	                cost_limited = True
1466	                continue

1468	            h = heuristic(nxt)

1470	                open_heap,
1471	                (new_g + h, h, nx, ny, next_t, new_g, new_path,
1472	                 seen | {nxt}),
1473	            )
1474	        if (allow_wait and wait_last is not None and next_t <= wait_last
1475	                and (x, y) not in frame and (x, y) not in reserved):
1476	            # Waiting in place: the route stays one more frame at no
1477	            # entering-cell cost. Only generated while the next time step
1478	            # still lies within the provided frames (after the last frame
1479	            # moves reuse it but no waits are generated), and only while
1480	            # the cell itself is free at that next frame. The coordinate

1482	            wait_path = path + ((x, y),)
1483	            h = heuristic((x, y))

1485	                open_heap,
1486	                (g + h, h, x, y, next_t, g, wait_path, seen),
1487	            )
1488	    if best_key is None:
1489	        result = {"path": None, "cost": None, "expanded": closed_count}
1490	        if has_status:
1491	            result["status"] = _status_for(budget_stop, cost_limited)
1492	    else:
1493	        best_g, _, best_path = best_key
1494	        result = {
1495	            "path": list(best_path),
1496	            "cost": best_g,
1497	            "expanded": closed_count,
1498	        }
1499	        if has_status:
